status_note: Real EXTERNAL native-Maven Java production adaptation to the POI 5 byte-cap, found by the pipeline and now CONFIRMED by a full 3-state differential through the real production ExcelParser.parse(). Upgraded from signature_confirmed on 2026-07-09 once the fixture was fixed: the break trips on an .xlsx whose sharedStrings.xml exceeds POI 5's 100,000,000-byte cap, built from DISTINCT, INCOMPRESSIBLE strings (see verification.why_now_reproduced).
discovery_method: bbc_e2e.py run poi-4.1.2-to-5.x -> mine-commits q='poi setByteArrayMaxOverride' -> classify (native Maven, production). Top *-ranked Maven candidate.

behavioral_break.mechanism: POI 5.0 introduced a default IOUtils byte-array cap; allocating past it during record/stream parsing throws org.apache.poi.util.RecordFormatException at runtime. Compiles fine -> behavioural. Fix: IOUtils.setByteArrayMaxOverride(n) (POI-5-only API).

adaptation.commit_message: Fix(parser): Increase Excel file size limit
adaptation.in_repo_causal_evidence: Added with the comment 'Override POI's default limits to handle large files' in the production parse() method.
adaptation.summary: Raised POI's byte-array cap to 200MB in the production Excel parser to handle large files under POI 5's new default limit.

verification.method: 3-state differential RUN on the real production source (ExcelParser.parse -> WorkbookFactory.create) via the repo's own Maven pom, JDK 17, surefire argLine -Xmx3g. States 1&2 use the parent code (7d6ffdd3); state 3 uses the adapted code (156a9624). State 1 downgrades all 3 org.apache.poi artifacts to 4.1.2 in the pom.
verification.test: bbc.PoiBbcTest (authored, JUnit5) — builds an .xlsx whose sharedStrings.xml is ~135MB from 4500 DISTINCT, INCOMPRESSIBLE strings, then calls the production ExcelParser.parse(). Preserved in scratchpad/poi-jadhavspeaks-harness/.

states.name: 2_new_lib_old_code
states.detail: org.apache.poi.util.RecordFormatException: Tried to read data but the maximum length for this record type is 100,000,000.

verification.differential_status: CONFIRMED — baseline passes, the same parent code breaks only under POI 5 with the byte-cap RecordFormatException, and the production override resolves it.
verification.why_now_reproduced: The earlier attempt used a ~75MB .xlsx whose 25 cells all held the SAME large string. Two flaws: (1) XSSF shared-string DEDUP collapsed it to one ~3MB entry, and (2) 75MB is under POI 5's 100MB default cap. The fix uses 4500 DISTINCT strings (no dedup) of random letters (INCOMPRESSIBLE, so the zip inflate-ratio / zip-bomb guard is not tripped first) totalling ~135MB in sharedStrings.xml. Reading via WorkbookFactory.create(InputStream) buffers that single zip part into a byte[] through IOUtils, which exceeds the 100MB cap -> RecordFormatException. The 200MB production override clears it.
gotchas: Repetitive/identical content trips POI's zip-bomb guard (RecordFormatException 'Zip bomb detected', MIN_INFLATE_RATIO 0.01) BEFORE the byte cap — the fixture must be incompressible so the part is genuinely >100MB uncompressed at a normal compression ratio.
Shared-string DEDUP: identical cell strings collapse to one SST entry, so the fixture must use DISTINCT strings.
verification.conclusion: Confirmed BBC: a real external native-Maven production adaptation. The parent code round-trips a large workbook on POI 4.1.2, the same code throws POI 5's byte-cap RecordFormatException, and the production IOUtils.setByteArrayMaxOverride(200MB) resolves it.
